svg.text: Every joint sits on a pin, a pad or a capacitor leg: no splices in mid-wire · LX-LBC3 charger with booster (sold as 'TP4056 Type-C 1.2A 2 in 1') · top view, motors at the front
● = solder joint · plain crossing = NO connection · ①–⑨ = power wires, see list
its legs go straight onto the DRV's VCC (+) and GND (−, stripe) pins
J1 jumper on the label side:
underside up (pins up), labels as printed on your board · USB end ← left wall, stays inside the case
3.7 V nominal · 4.2 V full · check polarity twice
④ + ⑧ on the same pin
4× keyboard switch · wire to the tagged NodeMCU pins
Don't hold A or D at power-on:
④ Other switch pin → DRV VCC
⑦ DRV GND → NodeMCU GND (the one next to Vin)
⑧ LED strip + → the same switch pin as ④
1000 µF: + on DRV VCC, − on DRV GND. Solder ④–⑦, ⑨ to its legs.
100 µF: + on Vin, − on the GND pin next to it.
100 nF ×2: across the two terminals of each motor.
SIGNAL, MOTOR AND LID WIRES (thin wire)
Use a different wire colour for each: they cross on the way.
OUT1 → left motor + · OUT2 → left motor −
OUT3 → right motor − · OUT4 → right motor +
IO0 → A · IO2 → D · IO13 → W · RX → S
NodeMCU GND (between IO14 and 3V3) → all four switches.
The status LED strip is on the case walls, not the lid:
it is wires ⑧ and ⑨.
Switch OFF: the cell charges, the robot stays off. Safe.
Switch ON: USB runs the robot and charges the cell. Safe;
the ESP may reboot once as the cable goes in or out.
Cable in the NodeMCU's inner USB: switch OFF first.
1. Cell on B+ / B− (check polarity), plug USB in once, unplug:
about 5 V on the charger's 5V holes.
2. Run both motors under load. The charger gives roughly
4. Go by the + / − printed on the charger, not the drawing.
